newsitem.title: USA: Avis franchise sued for discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Avis franchise sued for discrimination.

text.p: The Avis car rental agency came under fire on Tuesday from a Washington-based civil rights group that filed a class-action lawsuit against the company for discriminating against blacks.

The Washington Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights and Urban Affairs said the lawsuit alleges the owner of five franchises in the Carolinas instructed his employees to find reasons not to rent vehicles to African-Americans and that Avis corporate executives did not do anything to stop it.
So far 85 people were named plaintiffs in the case that dates back to 1986 and seeks an unspecified amount of damages, according to lead attorney John Relman.

Relman said the act was "a vicious, offensive pattern of discrimination over the last 10 years" and "a corporate culture of indifference among Avis executivs who were made aware of the problem and did nothing about it."
Franchise owner John Dalton was "unavailable" for comment, and a spokeswoman for Garden City, N.Y.-based Avis said officials were "preparing a statement."
